methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective comparison with a temporal switch design (sequential before Sept 2021, concomitant after) that confounds administration method with calendar time, antiemetic practice (aprepitant use 77.2% vs 84.0%), and treatment line (post-3rd-line 29.5% vs 16.0%). Baseline imbalance is severe: liver metastases 70.5% vs 34.0% (p<0.001) and metastatic recurrence 97.7% vs 74.0% (p=0.001), which the authors acknowledge but which undermine any causal claim about administration method on PFS/OS. No power calculation is reported, no propensity-score or stratified sensitivity analysis is performed, and the exclusion of patients who switched from sequential to concomitant creates informative censoring the authors concede (Discussion). Statistics are generally appropriate for descriptive comparison (Fisher, Mann–Whitney, Cox PH with assumption checked, log-rank), but no multiplicity correction is applied across many AE comparisons and multivariable models use a p<0.10 screen (an outdated stepwise approach) with CA19-9 producing uninterpretable HR 1.00 (95% CI 1.00–1.00); missing CA19-9/pathology handled by complete-case without sensitivity analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study (Oxford 2b) comparing two administration schedules of an established regimen at a single Japanese center. The clinical question — whether concomitant infusion of nal-IRI with Levo-LV preserves safety/efficacy while reducing chair time — is operationally relevant and addresses the increasingly discussed concept of 'time toxicity', with a plausible path to protocol change if confirmed. However, endpoints are standard (AEs, PFS, OS) rather than patient-reported time-burden measures, OS difference did not reach significance (HR 0.65, p=0.058), and confirmatory evidence is limited to one prior report [ref 12]; findings are hypothesis-generating and unlikely to independently change guidelines.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable standard for this retrospective observational cohort. Core items are present (eligibility, variable definitions, CTCAE v5.0, Cox PH assumption check, patient-flow Figure 2, numeric 95% CIs), and the limitations paragraph acknowledges selection bias and single-center scope. However, several STROBE items are weak or missing: no explicit discussion of how missing CA19-9/pathology was handled beyond 'no imputation', no sensitivity analysis, no description of how confounders were selected a priori, and the follow-up method is unclear (text calls patients 'randomized' — they were not). No data-availability or code-availability statement remains in the blinded manuscript, and no repository, protocol link, or supplementary material is referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: The core concept — simultaneous (parallel) infusion of nal-IRI alongside Levo-LV via a side branch — has already been reported by Takada et al. [ref 12], which the authors cite as showing safety and non-inferior efficacy. The present study is therefore an incremental single-center confirmation at a different Japanese institution, adding modest empirical replication (empirical novelty dimension) but no new mechanism, assay, population (same Japanese UR-LA/metastatic PDAC post-GEM setting), or trial design. The pharmaceutical pH-stability rationale is a reasonable addition but is drawn from publicly available drug monographs rather than new compatibility testing (the authors explicitly note they did not perform liposome denaturation blood sampling).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable and follows IMRaD structure; the abstract is quantitatively grounded and self-contained, acronyms are generally defined on first use, and figure captions describe the comparison adequately. However, several presentation issues weaken the paper: the Results refer to 'all randomized patients' though this is a retrospective cohort (terminology error), the abstract duplicates its conclusion sentence verbatim, and the CA19-9 Cox result is reported as HR 1.00 (95% CI 1.00–1.00) without rescaling (e.g., per 100 U/mL), rendering it uninterpretable. Table 4 is reduced to a single-line caption, and Figure 3 caption is imprecise about which group is on which side; the Discussion also leans heavily on restating results rather than contextualizing against ref 12.

key_strengths: Addresses a practically relevant operational question (infusion time/time toxicity) in a guideline-recommended regimen
Clear statistical reporting of HRs with 95% CIs, log-rank p-values, and verification of Cox PH assumption
Patient-flow diagram, pre-defined eligibility criteria, and CTCAE v5.0-graded AEs with explicit cut-off date
Pharmacologic pH-stability rationale provides a plausible mechanistic justification for concomitant infusion
key_concerns: Temporal switch design (Sept 2021) confounds administration method with antiemetic practice, treatment-line distribution, and era-of-care effects
Severe baseline imbalance — liver metastases 70.5% vs 34.0% (p<0.001), metastatic recurrence 97.7% vs 74.0% — not addressed by propensity scoring or stratification
Exclusion of patients who switched sequential→concomitant produces informative selection acknowledged but not quantified
Incremental novelty: parallel/concomitant administration already reported by Takada et al. (ref 12); present study is a single-center replication
Multivariable Cox used p<0.10 screening (outdated stepwise approach); CA19-9 HR 1.00 (1.00–1.00) uninterpretable without rescaling; no multiplicity correction across AE comparisons
No data/code availability statement; terminology error calling the retrospective cohort 'randomized patients'
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently reported but methodologically limited single-center retrospective cohort confirming a previously described concomitant administration schedule. Baseline imbalance, temporal confounding, and lack of propensity adjustment combined with modest novelty place this in Tier 4; minor revisions could address terminology, data-sharing, and rescaling of CA19-9 in the Cox model.
